entities.name: PMID:27503696
observations: Retrospective cohort of 626 revision THAs: 120 septic and 506 aseptic cases.
Septic revisions had higher crude transfusion (90% vs 73%) and mean blood loss (2533±161 vs 1974±68 mL).
After regression adjustment, infection was not independently associated with transfusion (P=0.176) or blood loss (P=0.437).

entities.name: PMID:31146563
observations: Retrospective cohort of 3264 revision THAs evaluating intravenous tranexamic acid.
Transfusion decreased from 49% to 18% in aseptic revisions and from 73% to 53% in septic revisions with tranexamic acid.
The study supports higher baseline transfusion in septic cases but was not a clean septic-versus-aseptic causal analysis.

entities.name: Periprosthetic joint infection
observations: Septic indication for revision THA is associated with higher crude blood loss and transfusion in available retrospective cohorts, but infection was not independently associated after adjustment in the strongest direct comparative study.

entities.name: Infection-independent bleeding risk
observations: In revision THA, the observed excess bleeding and transfusion in septic cases may be explained by revision complexity, age, ASA score, preoperative hemoglobin, and related factors rather than infection itself.
